messages.subject: FYI: new version of strapply
parts:
Hi all

This is to let you all know that Gabor Grothendieck, whose great
library gsubfn I discuss in QCLWR, has updated the function strapply
and made it considerably faster. Here's pretty much what he told me:

###
Hi, There is a new development version of strapply whose main purpose
is performance. It can be run like this:

library(gsubfn)
library(tcltk)
source("http://gsubfn.googlecode.com/svn/trunk/R/gsubfn.R")

There is more discussion on the home page <http://
gsubfn.googlecode.com> on the May 14th news item including the
remaining things that still have to be done but at this point most
examples will run so if you notice any problems I would appreciate
knowing about them. Internally it's a rather big change because the
core of strapply is now in tcl rather than R (this is transparent to
the user).
###

This should make some of the applications much faster!

Cheers,
STG
